latest_release.name: CCBaga 0.2.50
latest_release.body:
CCBaga combines recoverable local Claude identities, CLI management, real environment checks and an isolated companion browser.

| Platform | Installer |
| --- | --- |
| macOS Apple Silicon · A + B | [Download](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/download/v0.2.50/CCBaga-0.2.50-macos-arm64.dmg) |
| Windows x64 · A + B | [Download](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/download/v0.2.50/CCBaga-0.2.50-windows-x86_64-setup.exe) |
| Linux DEB | [Download](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/download/v0.2.50/CCBaga-0.2.50-linux-x86_64.deb) |
| Linux RPM | [Download](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/download/v0.2.50/CCBaga-0.2.50-linux-x86_64.rpm) |
| Linux AppImage | [Download](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/download/v0.2.50/CCBaga-0.2.50-linux-x86_64.AppImage) |
| Arch/pacman | [Download](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/download/v0.2.50/CCBaga-0.2.50-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst) |

Each installer contains both applications. On macOS drag both apps into Applications. On Windows run the setup installer; SmartScreen may show a warning because the installer has no Authenticode certificate. Organization policy can restrict installation.

Sidebar updates verify signed downloads: macOS updates A, Windows updates A and B. Linux uses its package manager. The archive and latest.json are used by automatic updates; ordinary installation only needs the platform installer. SHA256SUMS covers public downloads.

[Usage](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga#readme) · [Network Skill](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/tree/main/skills/ccbaga-network)

This release fixes local Claude identity round trips for generated debug pointers and configuration backups, strengthens browser profile ownership and region checks, and updates vulnerable application dependencies.

The companion engine remains pinned to Fingerprint Chromium 148.0.7778.215. Its fork-specific security backport coverage has not been independently verified; see the [security boundaries and audit record](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/blob/main/src-tauri/SECURITY.md).

detail.readme:
CCBaga

English · 简体中文

A native macOS, Linux and Windows toolkit for a cleaner workspace and an environment you can verify.

Claude identities · Browser fingerprints · System settings · Network Skill

Features · Installation · Updates · Quick start · Usage guide · Architecture · Development · Contributing

![CCBaga: native control, observable environments](docs/readme-hero.png) **Intended use:** CCBaga is intended solely for people residing or traveling abroad to manage their own Claude identities. Use that violates Anthropic's official terms of service is prohibited. CCBaga brings local maintenance and environment setup into one focused desktop workflow. Inspect Claude data before removing it, rotate your companion browser's fingerprint and restart it, align system settings with a selected region, and compare real browser readings with the machine and network exit. Two applications work together: **CCBaga-A** owns native operations; **CCBaga-B** runs an isolated Fingerprint Chromium profile. Browser measurements return to the host through a local session. Changing a setting and verifying its effect are separate steps. ## Features
Local Claude identities

Archive the current local identity, switch to a saved identity or start with an empty workspace. Choose what stays shared and what moves with each identity.		 Fingerprint & restart

Generate a fresh seed, apply the selected region's language and timezone, then restart the companion browser.		 Real environment checks

Compare browser and machine readings with the actual network exit. Passing measured checks produces a green page and a large checkmark.
Native system settings

Apply timezone, preferred language and region settings. Open desktop controls for location and permissions; see platform-specific limits.		 AI-guided network setup

Three simple steps, a coding-agent selector and a copyable Skill installation prompt. Give the AI your files and connection details; it handles the commands.		 Claude Code CLI tools

Detect the installation method and version. Uninstall or reinstall through native, npm/bun, Homebrew or WinGet workflows.
**One region selector. Four everyday actions.** Easy setup puts browser cache cleanup, fingerprint rotation, timezone/language reset and identity archiving on the same page. The sidebar keeps advanced controls in Network, Claude identities, Browser and Computer. The interface supports **English and Chinese**, with shared YAML catalogs. Switching the interface language does not change the computer or browser language. The bilingual **Usage guide** covers common actions and data boundaries. See the [full guide](docs/usage.md). ## Installation **Platforms:** macOS 12 or later on Apple Silicon; Linux x86_64 with GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1; Windows 10/11 x86_64. Intel macOS and Linux ARM64 are not supported. Linux x86_64 packages include DEB, RPM and AppImage built on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35), plus a separate package for current Arch/pacman systems. All include the companion browser. See [Linux setup](docs/linux.md) for installation and platform limits. Official versions are published exclusively by the project owner, **liseami**. Windows x86_64 uses one NSIS setup installer containing both A and B. The installer is not Authenticode signed and may show SmartScreen; managed security policy can block it. See [Windows setup](docs/windows.md) for installation, toolchains and platform behaviors. ### macOS Download the official installer from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/latest). The distribution package is named `CCBaga--macos-arm64.dmg`. It contains both applications: | Application | Installed bundle | Role | | --- | --- | --- | | CCBaga-A | `CCBaga-A.app` | Identity management, system settings and environment verification | | CCBaga-B | `CCBaga-B.app` | Companion browser with a dedicated profile | Download **one DMG**; it contains both applications. There is no separate browser download. The installer uses the same pixel-art style as this README. 1. Open the disk image and drag **both applications** into Applications. 2. Launch CCBaga-A. It starts the companion browser automatically. 3. Choose English at the bottom of the sidebar if needed. Source builds are available through the [development guide](#development). ## Updates Use **Check for updates** at the bottom of CCBaga-A’s sidebar. Startup checks quietly; installation only starts when you choose **Update and restart**. Downloads show actual progress and are verified before installation. Failed downloads can be retried; a failed restart does not download the update again. On **macOS**, in-app updates replace A; use the latest DMG to update both apps. On **Windows**, a verified NSIS update installs both A and B after closing this companion browser. On **Linux**, use the package manager or full package. ## Quick start ### Everyday setup Open **Easy setup**, select a country or region, then choose an action. Browser fingerprint rotation closes and restarts CCBaga-B, so save unfinished browser work first. Selecting a region changes language, timezone and regional settings; it does **not** change your public IP. ### Claude identities Open **Claude identities** to manage the local state of both Claude Code and Claude Desktop. Choose **Empty identity** to archive the current state before leaving a fresh workspace, or choose a saved identity to restore it. Every switch saves the outgoing identity first. Expand **Keep in workspace** to choose retention for skills and commands, plugins, MCP configuration, personal settings, project records, conversation history, and caches/logs. Login data always moves with an archived identity. Project source outside Claude's own data directories is not scanned. A confirmation names the outgoing identity and summarizes what stays in the workspace before closing recognized Claude processes. Portrait identity cards scroll horizontally with spring motion and subtle hover tilt. The white empty identity stays first, followed by the current local account with available name, email and organization information. **Save backup / Update backup** saves the selected current state while retaining the workspace, sign-in and browser binding. **Empty identity** archives the outgoing state before leaving a fresh workspace. Select a saved card to restore that identity. **Direct delete** removes selected current data without creating an archive; deleting a saved card removes only that archive. Both deletion actions require an explicit confirmation. Saved cards support password-protected **Export / Import** between devices with the same operating system. Import adds a saved identity without switching or overwriting existing accounts. Optional fingerprint settings exclude browser cookies, passwords and proxy settings; see [transfer limits](docs/identity-storage.md#move-a-saved-identity-to-another-device). Local plan/expiry badges are metadata, not server authentication results. A local SQLite database tracks names, policies and recovery state. Data is compressed into an authenticated, encrypted `.baga` container outside Claude's working directories. Archive verification precedes workspace changes; failed switches roll back, and an interrupted switch exposes recovery. Recovery also saves the pre-recovery state. Ordinary archive tools cannot open this container directly; filesystem ownership or administrator access is not an absolute secrecy boundary. Expired or revoked server-side logins may need authentication again. The app manages the default local directories, not every custom Claude profile. The program-maintenance controls uninstall or reinstall Claude Code without removing the identity vault. ### Browser verification Open **Browser** or the companion browser's local test page to measure the actual environment. Checks cover the network exit, country, timezone, language, platform, CPU count, engine version and location settings. **Clear cache** retains sign-ins and personal browser data. **Clear all browser data** permanently resets the current identity's entire browser profile, including saved passwords, encryption metadata, bookmarks, history, extensions, settings and website sessions. It requires a separate confirmation and creates no backup. Other identities' profiles and the identity vault are retained; the selected fingerprint configuration applies when the browser opens again. The success page appears only when the measured checks match, the report reaches the cleaner and no measurement error remains. **DNS and WebRTC leak checks are not independently verified.** A green result describes the measured checks, not a guarantee of anonymity or account acceptance. ### Network setup Open **Network** for three steps: **Get VPS → Get residential proxy → Install Skill**. Select **General**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, **OpenCode** or **Copilot**, then copy the installation prompt into your local coding agent. The prompt follows the app's English/Chinese setting. The [Network Skill](skills/ccbaga-network/README.md#installation) follows the Agent Skills specification and installs separately from the apps. It supports the npm `skills` CLI: `npx skills add liseami/CCBaga --skill ccbaga-network --global`; the AI selects the target tool, uses copy mode on Windows, and disables installer tracking. Give the AI your VPS address, the three matching PEM/PPK/PUB files or downloaded key bundle, and your residential SOCKS5 connection details. It handles file paths, private configuration, commands and checks; you do not need to open a terminal or edit JSON. Missing resources are purchased by you with the AI's guidance. Remote setup runs only after approval of the actual server changes. The Skill supports authorized Debian 12/13 servers using root key login on port 22. It checks the SSH identity and fixed SOCKS5 exit, configures Xray/Reality and delivers a private local import file after server self-checks pass. Client setup uses **TUN ON**, **System Proxy OFF** and an empty explicit browser proxy; actual TUN/browser verification remains a separate step. The subscription URL uses HTTP and contains credentials; prefer the file retrieved over SSH. Provider buttons link to [DMIT](https://www.dmit.io/aff.php?aff=28800) and [Webshare](https://www.webshare.io/?referral_code=qlm1mt9xibc9). Network setup is optional; local cleanup does not require a VPS or a proxy subscription. **The app does not collect SSH keys or proxy credentials and does not deploy to servers.** ## Architecture ![Pixel architecture map: native core, companion browser and a separate AI Network Skill](docs/architecture.svg) The UI owns inputs and presentation. Rust owns validation, task locks, process identity checks and execution. Small Objective-C bridges call macOS APIs; Rust Linux and Windows boundaries use native process identity checks and platform controls. The browser test page has no Tauri command access; it exchanges context and measurements through a random-token loopback session. | Layer | Technology | Responsibility | | --- | --- | --- | | Desktop host | Rust · Tauri 2 | Native commands, transactions, progress and lifecycle | | Interface | React 19 · TypeScript · Cromma UI | Forms, previews and execution results | | Platform bridges | AppKit · Security · CoreLocation · Linux / Windows Rust | Platform permissions and system integration | | Companion browser | Fingerprint Chromium | Dedicated profile and real browser measurements | | Separate Network Skill | Python standard library · OpenSSH · Bash · Xray | AI-managed private configuration, approved remote setup and server/client verification | | Localization | YAML · Vite | Build-time English/Chinese catalogs |
Repository map ```text assets/ Compressed brand logos and pixel-art DMG background src/ Desktop UI, browser test page and localization src-tauri/src/ Rust commands and transaction boundaries src-tauri/native/ Small macOS API bridges browser-runtime/ Engine metadata, launcher, entitlements and licenses scripts/ Icons, local builds and installation helpers skills/ Installable AI Network Skill and its execution scripts packaging/arch/ Native Arch Linux PKGBUILD and desktop entry docs/ README artwork and platform development guides vendor/cromma-ui/ Vendored interface components ``` The large browser application and archive are generated/runtime inputs, excluded from Git. `CLAUDE.md` files map module boundaries; source headers describe inputs, outputs and responsibilities.
## Development ### Prerequisites On Linux, follow [Linux setup](docs/linux.md). On macOS, use an Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode Command Line Tools, stable Rust and Bun. Follow [Tauri's macOS prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/#macos) for the native toolchain. The browser engine is an external build input. `python3 scripts/fetch-browser.py` downloads the pinned macOS arm64 **Fingerprint Chromium 148.0.7778.215** engine from the [upstream project](https://github.com/adryfish/fingerprint-chromium), verifies its SHA-256 and preserves its bundle structure and notices. Browser runtime binaries are not included in the source repository. From your checkout: ```sh bun install --frozen-lockfile python3 scripts/fetch-browser.py sh scripts/make-icons.sh sh scripts/package-browser.sh bun run tauri dev ``` Local builds are for development and testing; they are not official project downloads. ### Fast local build and install (macOS) ```sh bun run dev:install ``` This builds a debug app with the embedded UI, uses local ad-hoc signatures and installs/starts both apps. It does not use Apple credentials or create an installer. It preserves profiles and settings. The development installer accepts only locally built debug apps; downloaded installers still require the normal signature and Gatekeeper checks. ### Build ```sh MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0 \ bun run tauri build --bundles app --features custom-protocol ``` The host bundle is written to `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/CCBaga-A.app`. The companion bundle remains at `browser-runtime/Browser.app` until copied to Applications as `CCBaga-B.app`. Production builds require `custom-protocol` to load the embedded UI. Compilation without it fails explicitly, preventing an installed app from depending on the development server. ### Checks ```sh bun run build bun test MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0 \ cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml python3 scripts/test-sign-browser.py python3 skills/ccbaga-network/scripts/test_network.py bash -n skills/ccbaga-network/scripts/setup-vps.sh ``` Pull requests run the existing frontend, native Rust, offline Skill and npm skill-installation checks on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, plus the relevant platform regression tests. The workflow uses a read-only token, no signing secrets and no artifact uploads; it does not publish releases or download the browser engine. Complete engine and installer validation remains part of the separate delivery checks. The identity UI simulation uses 40 fictitious accounts, mocked Tauri IPC and an isolated headless context with external requests blocked. It covers card navigation, retention choices, switching, irreversible-delete alerts, failure recovery and both languages. Run `bun run test:identities` with Node.js 22.23.2 or later after preparing the pinned browser engine. The browser receives a temporary HOME/XDG configuration. Native archive tests use temporary SQLite databases and files; the macOS credential bridge is also checked against a separate disposable Keychain. Automated tests exercise disposable fixtures and local test servers. They do not deploy a real VPS, delete your Claude account data or perform administrator-authorized system changes. Real SSH connectivity, client-side TUN routing and permission-dependent operations require validation in the target environment. ## Data & permissions - **Identities are local.** Login state is archived before switching. You choose which personal data stays in the workspace and which is stored with the identity. Actual project source and cloud-side account records are outside this scope. - **Secrets stay out of UI logs.** The apps have no SSH key picker or server deployment command. After explicit confirmation, the native identity vault reads only the recognized default Claude credentials needed for restoration; credential contents never enter the GUI, command-line arguments or network. The separate Skill uses private local files and temporary private PEM copies (0600 on POSIX, verified user-only NTFS ACLs on Windows); data supplied to your coding agent is subject to that agent provider’s handling. - **Network checks make real requests.** Exit detection uses `ipwho.is` with `ipapi.co` as a fallback on the same route. IP location is a service estimate. - **Remote changes are explicit.** The separate Skill contacts only the VPS you provide after server-change approval. Required credentials remain in private local/server configuration, outside Git and public logs. - **Permissions are feature-specific.** Timezone changes require macOS administrator authorization. Keychain access follows system prompts. Location controls may require Accessibility permission or a manual action in System Settings. Custom `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` locations are not automatically included in the default identity scope. The app reports this limitation rather than silently claiming they were switched. ## Contributing Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Small, focused changes with clear behavior and relevant checks are welcome. For bug reports, include the operating system and version, app version, operation and sanitized error; never attach private keys, passwords or subscription URLs. ## License & credits CCBaga's original project code is released under the **[MIT License](LICENSE)**. Third-party code and binaries retain their own terms; see [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). Built with [Tauri](https://tauri.app/), [React](https://react.dev/) and [Fingerprint Chromium](https://github.com/adryfish/fingerprint-chromium), with a native macOS implementation of Claude maintenance workflows. Cleanup discovery was informed by the [claude-cleanup skill](https://github.com/suyuan2022/suyuan-skill/tree/main/claude-cleanup).
An independent project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or Apple.

# CCBaga

[English](README.md) · **简体中文**

CCBaga 是面向 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 的本地工具，用于管理 Claude 身份、伴生浏览器指纹与系统环境，并核验实际浏览器环境。**CCBaga-A** 负责本机操作，**CCBaga-B** 是使用独立资料目录的伴生浏览器。

**用途声明：**本项目仅供旅居海外人员管理本人的 Claude 身份；禁止违反 Anthropic 官方用户协议的用途。本地设置不会更改服务端记录，也不能保证匿名或账号可用。

本页提供简明中文导航；完整功能、开发步骤和平台限制见[英文 README](README.md)。应用界面和侧栏的「使用说明」均支持中文，可在侧栏底部切换语言。

## 安装

从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/latest) 下载由项目所有者 **liseami** 发布的官方安装包。

- **macOS 12+，Apple Silicon：**下载包含 A、B 两个应用的 DMG，将两者拖入 Applications，然后启动 CCBaga-A。详见 [macOS 安装说明（英文）](README.md#macos)。
- **Linux x86_64：**提供基于 Ubuntu 22.04（glibc 2.35）的 DEB、RPM、AppImage，以及面向当前 Arch 的 pacman 包，均包含伴生浏览器。依赖与限制见 [Linux 说明](docs/linux.md)。
- **Windows 10/11 x86_64：**使用包含 A、B 的 NSIS 安装器。安装器未进行 Authenticode 签名，可能出现 SmartScreen 提示或被组织策略阻止。详见 [Windows 说明](docs/windows.md)。

## 常用操作

- **傻瓜设置：**选择国家或地区后执行所需操作；地区设置不会改变公网 IP。
- **Claude 身份管理：**保存备份或切换本地身份，并选择保留哪些工作区资料；保存备份不改变当前工作区或浏览器绑定。可用密码加密包在同系统设备间导出/导入保存身份，不迁移网页登录。切换前保存工作；直接删除不可撤销且不会新增备份。
- **浏览器环境：**仅清缓存保留登录；全清理永久删除当前身份的密码、书签、历史、扩展、设置和站点数据，无备份，需单独确认。换指纹会重启 CCBaga-B；绿色核验仅代表已测项目匹配，不包含独立 DNS/WebRTC 泄漏验证。
- **电脑环境：**分别调整时区、语言与地区；部分操作需要系统授权、重启或注销。
- **网络环境：**复制提示词，让本地 AI 工具安装独立的 Network Skill。应用不收集 SSH 密钥或执行服务器部署，远端变更需单独确认。

- [使用速查（英文）](docs/usage.md)与[身份存储和恢复边界](docs/identity-storage.md)
- [更新说明（英文）](README.md#updates)
